$comment: THE DOOR REGISTER — every subtractive/admitting heuristic in the capture and propose paths, named, premised and receipted. Byte-stable and sorted by id; regenerate nothing, edit by hand and run npm run door-register:check. See spec/DOOR-REGISTER.md.

doors.premise: Uniform computed position:absolute across present combos is an overlay fact.
doors.effect: Admits declared position absolute.
doors.counterExample: Silent write; a harness-induced absolute is declared as design.

doors.premise: Width equal to height in every enabled combo at two or more distinct sizes means an authored 1:1 aspect.
doors.effect: Admits declared aspect-ratio 1 / 1.
doors.counterExample: Two sizes that coincidentally square mint an aspect lock.

doors.premise: A node with transparent background, no border and no shadow draws nothing, so unwrapping it loses no ink.
doors.effect: Drops wrapper/theme/display:contents nodes from the root chain.
doors.counterExample: isBoxlessNode tests only border-TOP and border-BOTTOM width, so a left/right-only bordered wrapper reads as boxless and is unwrapped; display:contents hosts are skipped unconditionally.

doors.premise: A display keyword outside the carried vocabulary has no carriage, and a display that varies across combos has no per-axis spelling.
doors.effect: Drops the display fact.
doors.counterExample: The residue is receipted; the admitting writes are silent.

doors.premise: div, and text-bearing span, are the emitter's defaults so the tag need not be carried.
doors.effect: Drops the element tag for those cases.
doors.counterExample: An emitter whose default is not div renders the wrong element.

doors.premise: A child whose computed width equals its row-flex parent's content width in every enabled combo is meant to span.
doors.effect: Admits layout.grow = true.
doors.counterExample: astryx harness hug width: the parent chain terminates at the harness stage, so a component that fills a 900px stage mints grow as if the library declared it. A block parent silently never mints.

doors.premise: A grid item ignores flex-grow on DOM and on canvas, so minting it would be a dead fact.
doors.effect: Drops flex-grow from minting for every child of a grid parent.
doors.counterExample: A part that later lowers to flex loses its grow.

doors.premise: A declared track list that disagrees with computed geometry beyond 0.5px is not authoritative.
doors.effect: Drops the declared candidate; computed truth wins.
doors.counterExample: A declaration correct at another width loses to a harness-width measurement.

doors.premise: If the used box equals the intrinsic track sum, the box IS its content and the canvas may hug it.
doors.effect: Admits literals width/height = fit-content, or a literal px.
doors.counterExample: astryx harness hug width: when the stage sizes the box to exactly that sum, the harness width is minted as HUG.

doors.premise: dense/column flow, subgrid, minmax, percent, auto-fit, zero tracks and 2-D grids have no auto-layout spelling.
doors.effect: Drops the whole layout for that part.
doors.counterExample: A simple two-column grid with a percent track is refused whole.

doors.premise: Chromium's resolved template includes implicit tracks and carrying them would rewrite the author's declaration.
doors.effect: Drops the structured grid promotion and falls back to flex lowering.
doors.counterExample: Any auto-flow grid loses its grid identity.

doors.premise: Anchors of a grid the contract does not carry are dead facts.
doors.effect: Drops the four grid placement longhands from minting.
doors.counterExample: A grid promoted later has no placement to recover.

doors.premise: A part that paints nothing in every combo, carries no ink, and whose every child is display:none is not anatomy.
doors.effect: Drops the part.
doors.counterExample: A childless paintless frame is deliberately left alone, so the rule is not symmetric.

doors.premise: A combo whose real-root count differs from the base cannot be aligned.
doors.effect: Drops the whole combo from the union.
doors.counterExample: A combo that legitimately renders two roots is discarded.

doors.premise: A part that paints nowhere must carry the fact that hides it or be refused.
doors.effect: Drops the part AND its whole subtree.
doors.counterExample: A part hidden by content-visibility that has painting children loses them too.

doors.premise: A defaultless enum that gates structure should gain its unset pseudo-value as a real enum value and the default.
doors.effect: Admits a new enum value and default into the public API surface.
doors.counterExample: The library's own API has no such value; the contract invents one.

doors.premise: An asset whose host part was refused belongs to nothing.
doors.effect: Drops the committed SVG file.
doors.counterExample: A glyph is deleted because its host failed a different door.

doors.premise: If neither presence nor its complement factors as a product, the part is a phantom.
doors.effect: Drops the part.
doors.counterExample: A part gated by a genuinely non-factoring condition is deleted.

doors.premise: A part's presence set must factor as a product of per-axis value sets or it is unspellable.
doors.effect: Drops the whole part upstream.
doors.counterExample: A part gated by a derived condition is deleted.

doors.premise: visibleWhen carries at most one boolean-true factor.
doors.effect: Drops the part.
doors.counterExample: A part gated by two booleans is deleted.

doors.premise: One Figma stroke paint: prefer colours of sides whose width is positive, and require them to agree.
doors.effect: Drops border colour when inking sides disagree.
doors.counterExample: shadcn global border-color plus a one-side width: with mismatched inking sides it returns the empty string and the ring loses its colour silently.

doors.premise: For a shape-leaf host, the parent's content box must equal the host's border box for offsets to bubble correctly.
doors.effect: Drops the decor part.
doors.counterExample: A padded host loses its decor.

doors.premise: Only content:"" decor boxes are canvas ink; an icon-font ligature glyph is not carriable.
doors.effect: Drops the pseudo.
doors.counterExample: Icon-font carets, chevrons and multiplication signs never reach the canvas.

doors.premise: The enabled plane is what the canvas draws; the disabled plane's differences are residue.
doors.effect: Drops disabled-plane paint and geometry from the carried decor.
doors.counterExample: A disabled-only decor is residue.

doors.premise: Paints means background alpha above zero, or a positive-width positive-alpha border, at absolute position, opacity above 0.05.
doors.effect: Drops the pseudo box.
doors.counterExample: Gradient-only, shadow-only and outline-only decor is outside the grammar; the (0, 0.05] opacity band is treated as not-drawn.

doors.premise: Decor presence must factor per-axis, and a defaultless-axis gate is outside v1.
doors.effect: Drops the decor part.
doors.counterExample: A base-hidden decor has no carriage.

doors.premise: A coincident, transparent, shadow-only pseudo can be folded onto the host because a Figma node casts shadow from its own alpha.
doors.effect: Drops the pseudo part and admits literals box-shadow on the host.
doors.counterExample: A pseudo offset by a sub-pixel is folded onto the wrong box.

doors.premise: The decor grammar carries background alpha and border rings only.
doors.effect: Admits the box and drops its box-shadow.
doors.counterExample: A glowing decor ring loses its glow.

doors.premise: Only translate, orthonormal rotate and uniform scale are carriable.
doors.effect: Drops the pseudo entirely.
doors.counterExample: A skewed decor is dropped whole.

doors.premise: Offsets, size, paint and rotation must each be uniform or a function of exactly one enum axis.
doors.effect: Drops the decor part at four separate fences.
doors.counterExample: A two-axis decor product has no spelling.

doors.premise: Computed truth beats the static extraction's source-read layout display.
doors.effect: Drops the reviewed display.
doors.counterExample: A harness-induced display overrides a reviewed one.

doors.premise: Flex-only fields are schema-invalid with display grid, so the reviewed layout is replaced wholesale.
doors.effect: Drops the entire reviewed layout object.
doors.counterExample: Every reviewed alignment decision is discarded when a root lowers to grid.

doors.premise: A decor box uniform across every enabled combo is measured truth, so the human-curated numbers are wrong.
doors.effect: Drops the reviewed shape width/height and admits the computed box.
doors.counterExample: A harness-derived decor box overwrites a reviewed design number.

doors.premise: Clipping to 1px is visually identical to display:none; AT semantics ride the contract.
doors.effect: Admits the part with declared display none and drops its children.
doors.counterExample: A visually-hidden live region's children are deleted.

doors.premise: clip-path inset(50%), the 1px clip box, clip rect(0,0,0,0) or opacity:0 mean visually hidden.
doors.effect: Admits an sr-only suffix into the union signature, changing alignment identity.
doors.counterExample: opacity:0 is a broad net: a genuinely zero-opacity animating part takes the sr-only identity.

doors.premise: The contract declares a STATE with no matching prop, so the factor has no spelling.
doors.effect: Drops the presence factor; the part renders in that plane anyway.
doors.counterExample: A disabled-only adornment renders everywhere.

doors.premise: A reviewed static part with no rendered counterpart in any captured combo would be phantom ink.
doors.effect: Drops the human-reviewed part.
doors.counterExample: A part rendered only under an unenumerated prop is deleted from the contract.

doors.premise: Element-tag-only evidence is too weak to hand a captured node a human-reviewed name.
doors.effect: Drops every element-only rejoin candidate.
doors.counterExample: Only the successful rejoin pushes; every rejection is invisible.

doors.premise: Per-value glyph assets are carriable only when markup is a function of exactly one axis.
doors.effect: Drops the icon asset.
doors.counterExample: An icon varying on size AND variant has no glyph.

doors.premise: A fill or stroke equal to the svg's inherited color is currentColor in spirit.
doors.effect: Rewrites the literal colour to currentColor so the concrete colour never lands in the asset.
doors.counterExample: polaris page-inherited ink: ink that arrives by inheritance from the PAGE is rewritten to currentColor, and on a generated surface with no page context the glyph draws black.
doors.closedNote: One line per discarded literal colour per asset, naming the value the fold threw away and the inherited colour it matched. The rewrite is unchanged.

doors.counterExample: A dashed border-style icon loses its dashes.

doors.effect: Drops the whole icon asset; the part is still promoted as a box.
doors.counterExample: Any rect/polygon/use icon has no glyph.

doors.premise: One host has one glyph plan.
doors.effect: Drops every later svg under the same host.
doors.counterExample: A two-icon host loses the second glyph.

doors.counterExample: None known; a backstop.

doors.effect: Drops the element from reconstruction and admits the asset.
doors.counterExample: None known; a repair.

doors.effect: Drops every descendant part and its styled channels.
doors.counterExample: A styled <g> inside the glyph loses its own paint, silently.

doors.premise: viewBox is not a computed style, so it can be reconstructed from computed size, path extent, or a sibling capture.
doors.effect: Admits an invented viewBox number.
doors.counterExample: A reconstructed box that is wrong scales the whole glyph.

doors.effect: Admits new union parts and keeps existing order.
doors.counterExample: Two sibling elements with identical stems are fused.

doors.counterExample: A library whose whole token layer arrives via @import is captured against a page that never loaded it.

doors.premise: A value equal to the UA BASELINE control for this tag — the same bare element measured on a page carrying the browser, the colour-scheme and the stage box and NOTHING the library ships (`capture.captureUaControls`) — is a user-agent default, not this component's fact, and the emitted surface inherits it for free. CUSTOM PROPERTIES (`--*`) are the one deliberate narrowing: they keep the IN-PAGE baseline, because a `:root` token block inherits onto every element in the page and a custom property paints nothing on its own — the channels it FEEDS are what this door measures.
doors.effect: Drops EVERY admitted channel equal to that baseline. Still the single largest subtraction in the pipeline: 246,318 (part, channel) pairs across the committed corpus. doors.counterExample: Two channels the UA baseline still cancels wrongly. (1) A library-authored value that COINCIDES with the user agent's own default equals the UA control and is dropped, even though the library declares it — 133 such drops corpus-wide, 23 of them in antd, which is 4 MORE than the in-page baseline dropped. (2) A `--*` custom property keeps the in-page baseline by construction, so one the library defines page-globally and the component re-declares identically is still dropped. The failure this door was named for — shadcn's `* { border-color: var(--border) }` cancelling the Input's real border-colour and Polaris' provider ink cancelling its text — is CLOSED by the UA baseline and pinned by the conformance cases `page-global-star-rule` and `page-inherited-ink`; shadcn's authored drops fell 103 to 1.

doors.premise: Column width and row height are box-model facts, not deltas from a <span> control baseline.
doors.effect: Admits width+height unconditionally on admitted cells.
doors.counterExample: A cell whose size IS the harness's is admitted anyway.

doors.premise: The table box model gives every cell the row's height; the cell's own computed height is a content-height lie.
doors.effect: Replaces the cell's height with the row's outer height.
doors.counterExample: A cell with its own explicit height loses it to the row.

doors.premise: Column identity is index-within-row; the anatomy has no colgroup/colspan concept.
doors.effect: Drops width+height for EVERY cell of the whole table.
doors.counterExample: Any colspan in the corpus disables column widths table-wide.

doors.premise: The stage width is pinned, so table-layout:auto reflow does not falsify the number.
doors.effect: Admits width (and height) for cell parts.
doors.counterExample: A table wider than the stage reflows and the stage width is minted.

doors.premise: If the column algorithm produced one width, all rows agree within 0.5px in every combo.
doors.effect: Drops width/height for that column; hugging cells is the fallback.
doors.counterExample: Sub-pixel rounding across many rows disqualifies a real column width.

doors.premise: A column width that is not a bare px length cannot be judged.
doors.effect: Drops width/height for that whole column.
doors.counterExample: A percentage-width column loses its size.

doors.premise: A table box's size comes from the lowered flex stack, never from the overlay-cluster admission.
doors.effect: Drops all GEOM_ADMIT channels from table-display parts.
doors.counterExample: A fixed-size cell inside a modal loses its box.

doors.premise: A part containing non-empty text has font-metric-dependent width, so its box is environment-coupled.
doors.effect: Drops ALL geometry channels from text-bearing parts inside an overlay component.
doors.counterExample: A fixed-width label inside an overlay stack loses its authored width.

doors.premise: Context-inherited typography IS the rendered truth; generated surfaces have no library body to inherit from.
doors.effect: Admits font-size/line-height/font-weight/font-family on text parts even when control-equal.
doors.counterExample: Deliberately unguarded by admit(), so it can re-add a channel the viewport door refused.

doors.premise: A dimension the library's own stylesheet binds to a CSS var is a design value, not a measurement.
doors.effect: Admits width/height on token-bound parts.
doors.counterExample: A token whose value is itself a percentage of the harness re-enters through the name.

doors.premise: The v14 no-two-entries rule spans tokensByProp and literalsByProp.
doors.effect: Drops the computed token.
doors.counterExample: A reviewed literal beats a measured token ref.

doors.premise: Same rule, within tokensByProp.
doors.effect: Drops the computed token.
doors.counterExample: A stale reviewed map masks the measured one.

doors.premise: resolveTokens merges in order and later wins, so defaultless-axis maps must sort after defaulted ones.
doors.effect: Admits the named plane over its own fallback.
doors.counterExample: Order is a convention the emitters must keep.

doors.premise: A combo carrying no translate is AT REST, not unobserved.
doors.effect: Admits translate-x/y across the whole enabled plane once any combo shows motion.
doors.counterExample: A part unobserved on some plane is asserted to be at 0px.

doors.premise: The bounded translate grammar covers every honest case; anything else is a non-translate transform.
doors.effect: Drops synthetic translate-x/y for that part entirely.
doors.counterExample: A rotate+translate thumb loses its motion.

doors.premise: A config-declared triage rule turns a contradiction into an accepted, named cause.
doors.effect: Removes the row from untriaged so it stops blocking.
doors.counterExample: A triage rule written too broadly hides a real contradiction.

doors.premise: A mint binding with a null ref is uncorrelated across planes.
doors.effect: Drops the token binding.
doors.counterExample: A three-axis colour loses its binding entirely.

doors.premise: A part is overlay anatomy only if position:absolute in EVERY enabled default combo.
doors.effect: Gates the whole geometry admission (width/height/insets/translate) for the cluster.
doors.counterExample: MUI Slider's thumb is static in one size variant, so the whole overlay cluster loses geometry.

doors.premise: With only one observed font-size an em-fold is indistinguishable from a uniform value.
doors.effect: Admits (mints) a uniform px value rather than folding.
doors.counterExample: A single-size component's em tracking is minted as px and stops scaling.

doors.premise: A part is a table box only if its computed display is the same table-* value in every enabled combo.
doors.effect: Admits into 'lowered', which then subtracts cluster geometry.
doors.counterExample: A responsive table that switches to display:block in one combo loses its table treatment.

doors.premise: Only color/px/number/shadow/gradient shapes plus the declared registry are carriable.
doors.effect: Drops the channel as "no schema channel today" (705 corpus-wide).
doors.counterExample: Every genuinely new fact class lands here and stays.

doors.premise: No single-capture arithmetic proves a positioner-written translate is harness-coupled, so refusing would be a hunch.
doors.effect: Admits translate-x/y on a viewport-resolved part.
doors.counterExample: A tooltip positioner's harness offset is minted as design motion.

doors.premise: A number that is a function of the harness window is not a library fact.
doors.effect: Drops left+right (+width) and top+bottom (+height) at every downstream door.
doors.counterExample: A genuinely full-bleed banner loses its width.

doors.premise: Vendor-prefixed longhands are Chromium's internal mirrors of standard channels.
doors.effect: Drops every -webkit-* channel.
doors.counterExample: -webkit-line-clamp is the only cross-browser two-line truncation and it evaporates.

doors.premise: A part with no element in ANY __default alignment is carried nowhere.
doors.effect: Drops every channel of that part.
doors.counterExample: An interaction-only part is carried on no plane at all.

doors.premise: Comparing against the real render with different strings would score the strings, not the styling.
doors.effect: Admits fixedProps and sampleText as prop defaults.
doors.counterExample: The sample text's metrics become the component's metrics.

doors.premise: Only parts the enriched contract carries can be scored.
doors.effect: Drops every non-carried part's channels from cellsCompared entirely.
doors.counterExample: Silent return: the gate never records which parts it declined to score, so the denominator shrinks invisibly.

doors.premise: Colour notation is not colour: hex, rgba and oklch of the same paint are equal.
doors.effect: Admits equality across notations in the divergence check.
doors.counterExample: A colour space conversion that is lossy is scored equal.

doors.premise: Two spellings that resolve to the same literal are a re-anchoring, not a regression.
doors.effect: Drops equal-resolving divergences from the findings set.
doors.counterExample: A rename that will diverge under another mode is scored equal.

doors.premise: Nothing compared is not a score. 0/0 cells is the ABSENCE of a measurement, not a perfect match.
doors.effect: Returns NULL for computed pctEqual when cellsCompared is 0, so the row enters no mean and no ">= 90%" / ">= 80%" tally. Until 2026-08-25 it admitted a fabricated 100 instead.
doors.counterExample: A null still says nothing about WHY every part was excluded upstream; the exclusion itself stays the upstream doors’ business.
doors.closedNote: The fabricated 100 is gone: a zero-cell comparison answers NULL, the same refusal the pixel side has always made for its own empty mean (gate.null-not-zero-means), and the scorecard names it in namedLosses. tailwind/Spinner is the one corpus row it moves.

doors.premise: Computed equality is exact string, no tolerance, never widened.
doors.effect: Admits or denies every cell.
doors.counterExample: A sub-pixel rounding difference scores as a full mismatch.

doors.premise: Our emitted svg wrapper is not like-for-like with the real svg; pixels judge glyphs.
doors.effect: Drops every channel of every icon part from computed equality.
doors.counterExample: Silent return.

doors.premise: A row that could not be driven into its interaction still scores, with the un-driven state, under a named note.
doors.effect: Admits an epistemically weaker row.
doors.counterExample: An un-driven hover row scores as if it were the hover plane.

doors.premise: The shipped contract can only see the DTCG tokens plus this run's fresh mint plus the shipped minted tree, fresh winning every collision.
doors.effect: Decides which token refs resolve at all, and therefore the whole computed percentage.
doors.counterExample: A fresh mint that is wrong silently replaces a correct shipped leaf.

doors.premise: Only a library's genuine first-ever pass may measure against an empty shipped tree.
doors.effect: Admits a leavesAdded zero measurement that is otherwise refused.
doors.counterExample: An allowlisted library never proves its tree grew.

doors.premise: Our render missing the selector is a MISMATCH, not a skip, and its channels still count.
doors.effect: Admits a selector mismatch row and counts all channels as compared.
doors.counterExample: None known; a repair.

doors.premise: A combo and state with no captured truth cannot be scored.
doors.effect: Drops the row from scoring and keeps it as no-original.
doors.counterExample: None known; a repair.

doors.premise: No original screenshot means there was never a pair at all.
doors.effect: Drops the row from pairs entirely.
doors.counterExample: None known; a repair.

doors.premise: In this metric 0 means PERFECT, so an empty mean must be null, never 0.
doors.effect: Admits null instead of a fabricated best score.
doors.counterExample: None known; a repair.

doors.premise: on/off axis values are boolean prop defaults driving visibleWhen and stylesWhen.
doors.effect: Admits presence axes.
doors.counterExample: A tri-state prop spelled on/off loses its third value.

doors.premise: rgb and rgba of the same paint at full alpha are the same paint.
doors.effect: Admits equality.
doors.counterExample: None known.

doors.premise: A mid-transition sample is not a fact, so the gate settles exactly as the capture does.
doors.effect: Admits only steady-state values.
doors.counterExample: No receipt of what settled or how long.

doors.premise: A wrong-sized box is a geometry failure, not a percentage.
doors.effect: Drops the row from measured and from the means, keeps it in pairs, and makes it structurally unable to be perfect.
doors.counterExample: None known; a repair.

doors.premise: Only disabled among the state props has a DOM spelling the emitted static HTML can be driven into.
doors.effect: Drops every other state prop's plane from being driven.
doors.counterExample: Only the unsupported-element case marks a DOM attribute, which is not in the scorecard.

doors.premise: Only channels the styled-channel door admitted are facts, minus webkit, geometry, logical aliases and synthetic translate.
doors.effect: Drops four families of channels from the denominator.
doors.counterExample: Every capture-side door's subtraction is inherited by the score without being named again.

doors.premise: The gate page must render against the library token stylesheet; an empty path is a config error, not a score.
doors.effect: Refuses the whole gate run by throwing.
doors.counterExample: Reaches stderr as a REFUSED line only.

doors.premise: No aligned truth element means nothing to compare.
doors.effect: Drops the part's channels from channelsCompared silently.
doors.counterExample: Contrast with the adjacent rule, which counts a missing selector as a MISMATCH.

doors.premise: A ref that cannot resolve is UNRESOLVABLE(v), never a throw.
doors.effect: Admits the row into the divergence table as unequal.
doors.counterExample: None known; a repair.

doors.premise: generateCss is the emitters' own referee for a dangling ref, so the census borrows it and never invents a rule.
doors.effect: Admits the render regardless and counts dangling refs.
doors.counterExample: Truncated to 40 in the scorecard, though the count is kept.

doors.premise: An unscored row is the worst kind of row, not a missing number to skip past.
doors.effect: Admits unscored rows to the top of worstRows.
doors.counterExample: None known; a repair.

doors.premise: An unset pseudo-value means no override renders.
doors.effect: Drops the axis override for that combo.
doors.counterExample: A default that should still apply is deleted.

doors.premise: A bounded sample is enough for a reader.
doors.effect: Drops the tail of the findings from the artifact.
doors.counterExample: worstRows and topMismatchedChannels keep no total, unlike unresolvedTokenRefs which does.

doors.premise: A part with no styled channels contributes nothing.
doors.effect: Drops the part from the row.
doors.counterExample: A part every door subtracted from scores as absent rather than as a loss.

doors.premise: Breakpoint-conditional styling has no contract channel.
doors.effect: Drops every media-scoped rule AND every custom-prop def inside one.
doors.counterExample: The comment says "named elsewhere (ledger)" but no push exists at either site.

doors.premise: CSS modules scope classes per file, so part rules are usually top-level with no root compound.
doors.effect: Admits a bare part rule as if it were root-then-part.
doors.counterExample: A global utility class matching a part name is promoted as that part's rule.

doors.premise: calc() over chain-resolved px or number literals is deterministic arithmetic; calc() over a token ref is a derived value, not a binding.
doors.effect: Admits an evaluated literal and drops token-valued and out-of-grammar calcs.
doors.counterExample: A themed calc loses its binding.

doors.premise: Four-decimal rounding is a faithful spelling of the result.
doors.effect: Admits a rounded value.
doors.counterExample: A value that needed more precision is silently rounded.

doors.premise: px times px and px plus a bare number have no CSS meaning.
doors.effect: Drops the calc.
doors.counterExample: The specific unit violation is folded into the generic out-of-grammar string.

doors.premise: A chain deeper than twelve hops is refused by name rather than followed.
doors.effect: Drops the binding.
doors.counterExample: A deeply themed token is refused.

doors.premise: A var chain landing on a same-package literal definition is deterministic and carriable with provenance.
doors.effect: Admits a literal the raw-literal door refuses, distinguished purely by chain length.
doors.counterExample: The distinction is chain length, not authorship.

doors.premise: Only descendant part selectors are promoted.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: A child-combinator part rule is lost.

doors.premise: Custom-prop definitions visible to a class context are the base-state, non-media ones.
doors.effect: Drops state-scoped and media-scoped definitions from the resolution environment.
doors.counterExample: A token redefined on :hover is invisible to resolution.

doors.premise: A custom-property declaration is a token declaration, not a rendered channel.
doors.effect: Drops every custom-property declaration from the winners.
doors.counterExample: Mirrors the computed-side rule, which DOES emit a receipt for the same premise.

doors.premise: A selector may nest at most root plus one part.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: A three-level part rule is lost.

doors.premise: An undefined var with a fallback resolves through the fallback.
doors.effect: Admits the fallback value.
doors.counterExample: A var undefined only in this context takes its fallback as the fact.

doors.premise: Only a comma list of plain classes inside :is() or :where() is promotable.
doors.effect: Drops other contents and admits the class-list form.
doors.counterExample: The zero-specificity property of :where() is not recorded.

doors.premise: A selector requiring classes absent from the context does not apply.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: missingClasses is computed as MULTI-AXIS evidence and then discarded entirely by its only consumer, so the evidence never reaches QueryOutcome.

doors.premise: A comma at paren depth zero is a multi-layer value whose shorthand semantics belong to the caller.
doors.effect: Neither admits nor refuses; hands the kind up.
doors.counterExample: If the caller ignores it the layers are lost with no refusal.

doors.premise: A var that resolves to no token and has no reachable definition in this class context is refused.
doors.effect: Drops the binding.
doors.counterExample: A var defined under a media query is unreachable here.

doors.premise: A class negation is answerable from the root class context; anything else is not.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: The non-match branch is silent; only the refusal branch is named.

doors.premise: A disabled negation excludes the disabled plane, no more.
doors.effect: Drops the rule on the disabled query only.
doors.counterExample: A plain non-match, not a named refusal.

doors.premise: One- and two-term padding shorthands map onto block and inline by CSS's own semantics; three- and four-term per-side longhands are not contract channels.
doors.effect: Drops three- and four-term shorthands.
doors.counterExample: The caller must refuse and name it; this site does not.

doors.premise: A part compound may carry only state pseudos and a disabled negation after the part selector.
doors.effect: Drops anything else.
doors.counterExample: A part rule with an attribute selector is lost.

doors.premise: Any other pseudo or attribute selector is not promotable.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: A data-attribute variant rule is lost.

doors.premise: A pseudo-element is not a contract channel.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: A ::placeholder colour is lost from the source layer.

doors.premise: A raw literal declaration is reported, never turned into an invented token.
doors.effect: Drops the binding.
doors.counterExample: A hand-written hex is never a token.

doors.premise: One refusal string per distinct cause is enough.
doors.effect: Drops duplicate evidence.
doors.counterExample: The strings survive; the per-rule counts do not.

doors.premise: A bare element selector at root position is not promotable.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: A library that styles by tag has no source layer.

doors.premise: A value mixing var() with other content is not a single binding.
doors.effect: Drops the binding.
doors.counterExample: A shadow built from several vars is lost.

doors.premise: A rule whose state differs from the queried state does not apply.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: Plain non-match.

doors.premise: A chain landing on a var whose hyphen-join resolves in the wrapped token tree IS a token ref.
doors.effect: Admits the ref; membership in the tree is the allowlist.
doors.counterExample: The ref itself is the only trace.

doors.premise: A rule cannot belong to two states at once.
doors.effect: Drops the rule.
doors.counterExample: A hover-and-focus rule is lost.

doors.premise: A var() cycle cannot resolve.
doors.effect: Drops the binding.
doors.counterExample: The full chain is named.

doors.premise: A shipped alias must stay a reference so the library's own stylesheet and modes still decide the value.
doors.effect: Admits a var() spelling.
doors.counterExample: Printed raw it is invalid CSS and a silent empty custom property; comment only.

doors.premise: Bool sides are spelled as root data-attribute selectors, a spelling nested parts do not have.
doors.effect: Drops bool axes from every nested-part classification.
doors.counterExample: The filter is silent; only a terminal none gets a reason.

doors.premise: Heavy repetition across cells is structure an arbitrary assignment would not show.
doors.effect: Admits either way and annotates.
doors.counterExample: Deliberately a hint, not a gate.

doors.premise: An unnameable value shape gets NO invented type rather than a wrong one.
doors.effect: Drops the type from sizing-keyword leaves.
doors.counterExample: Silently omitted.

doors.premise: The substituted ref must be a real tree prefix for every key, so suffixes are probed as a group.
doors.effect: Drops a group base.
doors.counterExample: Silent.

doors.premise: A leaf may not sit on another leaf's path because a group under a leaf would corrupt the DTCG tree.
doors.effect: Drops that path and retries with a suffix.
doors.counterExample: The retry is silent.

doors.premise: No minted name may be mistaken for a semantic token.
doors.effect: Admits every minted path under imported.*.
doors.counterExample: The prefix is the receipt; there is no ledger line.

doors.premise: A caller whose binding placer cannot spell a nested pair must never be handed one.
doors.effect: Drops pair classification for nested parts when the flag is off.
doors.counterExample: A capable caller that forgets the flag loses pairs.

doors.premise: A nested part's per-value map pins exactly one axis, leaving two placeholders.
doors.effect: Drops every nested triple.
doors.counterExample: A three-axis nested colour mints nothing.

doors.premise: An observation with no occurrences has nothing to mint.
doors.effect: Drops the observation.
doors.counterExample: None known.

doors.premise: Every fully-covered pair must be tried before any relaxed pass, or axis order alone trades a measured binding for a supplied one.
doors.effect: Admits the two-axis classification.
doors.counterExample: Only surfaced via the unwitnessed caveat.

doors.premise: A path claim with the same value and text style merges usage sites; a different value takes a numeric suffix.
doors.effect: Admits both and never overwrites a value.
doors.counterExample: The numeric suffix is the only trace; nothing names the collision.

doors.premise: A per-axis-value leaf takes the matching occurrence's style name, then the observation-level one, then none.
doors.effect: Admits an identity onto each axis leaf.
doors.counterExample: A wrong fallback attaches the wrong style name.

doors.premise: The fill must be a function of the contract's declared axis order, never the dump's arbitrary first occurrence.
doors.effect: Admits a specific supplied value.
doors.counterExample: The rank is a convention, not a measurement.

doors.premise: One genuinely-drawn-but-unobserved cell means the observation really is incomplete.
doors.effect: Drops the pair.
doors.counterExample: Silent continue.

doors.premise: Cells a Figma variant set proves it never realizes are not missing data.
doors.effect: Admits a pair whose holes are filled from a base observation.
doors.counterExample: A set that simply was not drawn looks the same as one that cannot be.

doors.premise: Occurrences at or below cell count means every cell holds at most one observation, so any values would fit.
doors.effect: Admits the pair with an epistemic warning.
doors.counterExample: A refusal here was measured as worse than the disease.

doors.premise: Saturation is a statement about drawn evidence, so supplied cells belong in neither denominator nor histogram.
doors.effect: Adjusts the caveat's numbers.
doors.counterExample: None known.

doors.premise: A literal used at three or more uniform usage sites is shared vocabulary; below three it stays a per-site leaf.
doors.effect: Routes into imported.shared vs a per-site path.
doors.counterExample: The only pure numeric threshold in the mint, and nothing names it or the two-site near miss.

doors.premise: A deduped literal's name is mechanical from its kind and value.
doors.effect: Admits a colour-family or scale name.
doors.counterExample: Two different design intents with the same value share one name.

doors.premise: Substituted refs expand over every declared enum value, so partial coverage would fabricate a dangling ref.
doors.effect: Drops an otherwise-fitting single-axis classification.
doors.counterExample: The terminal reason never says a single axis fit but coverage was partial.

doors.premise: A presence-shaped channel's unobserved combinations draw nothing, so the declared vacuous value closes the dangling-ref hole.
doors.effect: Admits a classification full coverage would refuse.
doors.counterExample: Unlike the ragged fill, a sparse fill attaches NO caveat, so filled cells are indistinguishable from measured ones.

doors.premise: A style-named leaf must not collapse into imported.shared and lose the designer's word.
doors.effect: Drops style-named leaves from the share threshold.
doors.counterExample: Silent.

doors.premise: A Figma text style is design-system vocabulary shared across components.
doors.effect: Admits a component-independent imported.text path.
doors.counterExample: The routing itself is silent; only an extensions block traces it.

doors.premise: Same value is not enough to merge: the text-style identity must match too.
doors.effect: Drops the merge and forces a suffixed sibling.
doors.counterExample: Silent.

doors.premise: Three placeholders maximum, root only, every combination observed with a single value.
doors.effect: Admits the three-axis classification.
doors.counterExample: An irrelevant axis can never ride along, so a near-fit falls through generically.

doors.premise: Values that differ across variants without correlating to any axis, pair or triple mint nothing.
doors.effect: Drops the whole observation; the binding stays null.
doors.counterExample: A four-axis design token has no carriage.

doors.premise: An identical value at every occurrence is one fact and one leaf.
doors.effect: Admits a single leaf.
doors.counterExample: Happy path; usageSites is the only trace of how many sites agreed.

doors.premise: Colours are lowercase hex, px-like numbers are px, and a size kind that is a keyword passes through verbatim.
doors.effect: Admits a canonical spelling.
doors.counterExample: A colour authored in oklch loses its gamut.

doors.premise: Slot parts refuse styling because the consumer owns the content box.
doors.effect: Drops the positioned wrapper.
doors.counterExample: An absolutely-placed slot renders in flow.

doors.premise: A spacer's whole job is in-flow growth.
doors.effect: Drops placement.
doors.counterExample: A spacer used as an overlay renders in flow.

doors.premise: Absolute placement only carries under a closed set of constraint and mint conditions.
doors.effect: Drops placement across six distinct premises.
doors.counterExample: A constraint outside the set renders the child in flow.

doors.premise: A declared literal has no per-variant vocabulary.
doors.effect: Drops the ratio.
doors.counterExample: A size-varying ratio is lost.

doors.premise: The child contract or slot content owns its box, and the lock acts on resize only.
doors.effect: Drops the lock.
doors.counterExample: A square avatar slot loses its ratio.

doors.premise: CONSUMED_BOUND_FIELDS is the complete contract vocabulary.
doors.effect: Drops bindings such as counterAxisSpacing.
doors.counterExample: A designer's bound row gap is discarded.

doors.premise: Every variant's bound ref resolves through the captured _variables layer, so literal fidelity substitutes for the ref.
doors.effect: Admits refs that refuse unification as per-variant literals.
doors.counterExample: The token identity is lost even though the paint survives.

doors.premise: A dump with no _variables cannot mint at literal fidelity.
doors.effect: Drops the paint channel.
doors.counterExample: A REST-sourced dump has no _variables and loses bound paints.

doors.premise: clipsContent not true means overflow visible.
doors.effect: Drops the clip.
doors.counterExample: Bare return; an unset field and a false field are the same.

doors.premise: On a set this pipeline did not draw, Figma's frame default is also true, so authored clip and untouched default are byte-identical.
doors.effect: Drops overflow hidden.
doors.counterExample: A foreign kit's genuinely clipping card loses it.

doors.premise: No per-variant vocabulary.
doors.effect: Drops the clip.
doors.counterExample: A scrolling variant loses it.

doors.premise: The child contract or slot content owns its own overflow.
doors.effect: Drops the clip.
doors.counterExample: A slot wrapper that must clip does not.

doors.premise: height 100% of an auto height is auto, so no grammar spelling is exact.
doors.effect: Drops the fill.
doors.counterExample: A full-height divider inside a hugging row loses it.

doors.premise: The cross-axis stretch has no per-variant spelling.
doors.effect: Drops the fill.
doors.counterExample: A size-gated stretch is lost.

doors.premise: The parent cannot carry align stretch for one part alone and the contract has no per-part align-self.
doors.effect: Drops the fill.
doors.counterExample: One stretching sibling among several loses it.

doors.premise: A box-shadow is one token, so per-channel bound refs have no carrier.
doors.effect: Drops the variable identity.
doors.counterExample: A themed shadow colour stops following the mode.

doors.premise: Only DROP_SHADOW maps to box-shadow; BLUR and INNER_SHADOW have no carrier.
doors.effect: Drops the whole effects channel.
doors.counterExample: An inner-shadow inset field loses its depth.

doors.premise: The state-diff door elsewhere owns default-bare / state-drawn shadow stacks, so this pass may stay quiet.
doors.effect: Emits nothing at all for the node's effects.
doors.counterExample: Bare return with no note; if that other door is off, the shadow vanishes silently. The premise is unverified here.

doors.premise: Effect styles have no token class in the contract grammar.
doors.effect: Drops the style identity and admits the resolved layers as literals.
doors.counterExample: The named elevation style is lost.

doors.premise: A node with no fill field and no capture receipt was DRAWN with no solid, so absence is an observation.
doors.effect: Admits variants with no fill as #00000000 so the whole background-color axis carries.
doors.counterExample: A pre-v1 dump that simply never recorded fills mints transparent everywhere.

doors.premise: A child's drawn px is environment-dependent geometry this pipeline does not read back or mint.
doors.effect: Drops the drawn size; the part sizes to content.
doors.counterExample: antd G8 fit-content: a hug that IS the design loses its number.

doors.premise: A bound var, abs placement or bbox already speaks for the dimension.
doors.effect: Drops the receipt too.
doors.counterExample: Bare continue; if the carrier later refuses, nothing names the dimension.

doors.premise: Mixed sizing modes across variants are not one fact.
